title.value: Handle small business accounting, ordering, and flyers with AI

introduction.value: A small business owner uses Claude and ChatGPT for accounting, ordering, and sales flyers, cutting workload by an estimated 30-40% while still reviewing for mistakes.

method.value: The owner says they run most of a small grocery-style store’s back-office work and now use both Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions across accounting, ordering, sales flyers, and even weekly employee schedules. The models handle drafts and updates while the owner does other tasks, but they still review the output closely because the AI makes mistakes and isn’t trusted to run the books unattended.

outcome.value: They estimate the tools cut their workload by about 30–40%, shrinking a day with 6–8 hours of real work to roughly 4–5 hours. They say it is a big net positive and has freed up more marketing, but it still needs direct oversight.

notes.value: Their stated cost was $20 for Claude plus $20 for ChatGPT per month, and they said that was fine for now versus buying local-model hardware.

Handle small business accounting, ordering, and flyers with AI
A small business owner uses Claude and ChatGPT for accounting, ordering, and sales flyers, cutting workload by an estimated 30-40% while still reviewing for mistakes.

What they did
The owner says they run most of a small grocery-style store’s back-office work and now use both Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions across accounting, ordering, sales flyers, and even weekly employee schedules. The models handle drafts and updates while the owner does other tasks, but they still review the output closely because the AI makes mistakes and isn’t trusted to run the books unattended.
How it went
They estimate the tools cut their workload by about 30–40%, shrinking a day with 6–8 hours of real work to roughly 4–5 hours. They say it is a big net positive and has freed up more marketing, but it still needs direct oversight.
Worth knowing
Their stated cost was $20 for Claude plus $20 for ChatGPT per month, and they said that was fine for now versus buying local-model hardware.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
I run a [type of] small business. I'll paste in [sales numbers, supplier price lists, or invoices] and need you to reconcile them, flag anything that looks off, and suggest a reorder list based on [stock levels or usual quantities]. Then write a one-page sales flyer for [promotion] in the tone of [brand voice]. Show your math and list anything you're unsure of so I can check it before I use any of it.
